entities.label: AgentObligationBinding
entities.rationale: An agent-obligation binding is an externally grounded normative relation that attaches to an agent by virtue of their position within a legal or social system. It is not internally grounded (ruling out Disposition) and is not merely a measurable property (ruling out Quality). It is most naturally typed as a Role: a specifically dependent continuant that inheres in a bearer (the obligated agent) and is grounded in the relational structure of a legal system. The existing working:LegalObligation class already captures obligation-as-role, so AgentObligationBinding should be modeled as a subclass of working:LegalObligation, which is itself typed under BFO_0000023 (Role).

relations.rationale: AgentObligationBinding is a species of LegalObligation: it is the specific binding of a legal obligation to a particular agent, individuating the obligation relative to its bearer. LegalObligation is already typed as BFO_0000023 (Role) and BFO_0000020 (Specifically Dependent Continuant), so this subclassing preserves BFO consistency.
Explicit assertion that AgentObligationBinding is a subclass of BFO Role, ensuring typing is traceable to BFO 2020 without relying solely on inheritance through LegalObligation.

open_questions: Should 'agent-obligation binding' be treated as a class (a kind of thing that many instances can fall under) or as a specific individual binding in a particular legal context (e.g., the obligation of a named person under a named statute)?

Is the 'agent' in 'agent-obligation binding' always a legal person (human or corporate), or can it include non-persons such as AI agents or states? This affects whether the bearer relation (RO_0000052 inheres in) should be restricted to a Person class.

Should AgentObligationBinding carry a correlative structure (i.e., every binding implies a right-bearer on the other side, per Hohfeld), and if so, should a relation to working:LegalRight be asserted?

Is the binding itself the role, or is the binding a process (BFO_0000015) by which the role comes to inhere in the agent? If the latter, a separate BindingProcess class under BFO_0000015 would be needed alongside the role.
proposal.rationale_summary: The phrase 'agent-obligation binding' denotes the normative tie that attaches a legal obligation to a specific agent as its bearer. In BFO terms, obligations that inhere in agents and are externally grounded in a legal or social system are Roles (BFO_0000023), a subtype of Specifically Dependent Continuant (BFO_0000020). The working ontology already contains working:LegalObligation typed as BFO_0000023/BFO_0000020; 'agent-obligation binding' is best modeled as a new class AgentObligationBinding that is a subclass of working:LegalObligation, capturing the individuating, agent-directed aspect of the obligation. No new BFO type is required; the classification is Role. Key open questions concern whether this is a class or individual, the scope of 'agent', potential Hohfeldian correlatives, and whether the 'binding' event should be separately represented as a Process.
